questions.question: In the discretized free regions, which constraint does requiring real lattice phase ϕ place on the original energy?

options.C: E is unrestricted if M is finite

questions.rationale: The relation 2 cosϕ=2−h²E and real ϕ imply the stated finite-difference band.
questions.evidence_quote: reality of the new energy variable ϕ imposes the constraint

questions.question: What does the paper identify as the actual innovation in its scattering construction?

options.A: Complexifying one potential-characterizing parameter within the discretized treatment
options.B: Replacing the Schrödinger equation with a relativistic dispersion relation
options.C: Using a nonlocal boundary condition instead of incoming and outgoing waves
options.D: Deriving a new definition of transmission unrelated to wave amplitudes

questions.rationale: The abstract frames the PT-symmetric extension as complexification of a potential parameter.
questions.evidence_quote: only innovation emerges in fact via a complexiﬁcation

questions.question: For the simplest cutoff M=1, what amplitudes result from the real central coupling Z₀?

options.C: C=eⁱϕ and B=0 for every Z₀

questions.rationale: Matching the three central equations gives these transmission and reflection amplitudes.
questions.evidence_quote: one identifies B = C −1 and gets the solution

questions.question: How is PT symmetry encoded in the finite-range lattice potential used in the matrix formulation?

options.A: The diagonal elements obey Sₖ=S*₋ₖ with an odd imaginary component iYₖ sign(k)
options.B: Every diagonal element is real and independent of k
options.C: The imaginary component is even under k→−k and the real part is odd
options.D: Only the boundary waves, not the interaction matrix, are PT symmetric

questions.rationale: The real Z profile is symmetric and the imaginary Y contribution changes sign across the origin.

questions.question: For cutoff M, what is the dimension of the reduced square system after prescribed exterior waves are removed?
questions.rationale: The matching reduction yields a tridiagonal square matrix and system of 2M−1 equations.

questions.question: Which inverse-matrix elements does the paper say suffice for the scattering amplitudes, while most of the partition is redundant?

options.A: The corner elements α and β of R=T⁻¹
options.B: The full interior block Q and all eigenvectors
options.C: Only the trace and determinant of the original infinite matrix
options.D: The first row vector t and last row vector w alone

questions.rationale: After eliminating internal wavefunction components, the amplitude equations depend on the corner parameters α and β.
questions.evidence_quote: knowledge of the other two column vectors ⃗u and

questions.question: What relation does the model give between β and the finite matrix T?
questions.rationale: The paper explicitly identifies β as the reciprocal determinant, while α shares that denominator.
questions.evidence_quote: β is equal to 1/ det T and α has the same denominator of course

questions.question: What complexity warning does the author give for explicit coupling formulas at M≥4?

options.A: At M=4, det T and the real and imaginary parts of γ already contain 15, 14, and 32 products, so symbolic computation is advised
options.B: At M=4 all three expressions vanish identically, requiring numerical regularization
options.C: The formulas remain linear in all couplings, so closed forms simplify with M
options.D: Only β becomes complex at M=4; α remains coupling-independent

questions.rationale: The displayed M=4 expansion grows rapidly and motivates computer symbolic manipulation for higher dimensions.
questions.evidence_quote: represented by the sums of 15 and 14 and 32 products of couplings, respectively.

questions.question: What central conclusion does the author draw about PT-symmetric scattering compared with Hermitian scattering?

options.A: The amplitude formulas keep the same form; the difference is carried by lattice-dependent α and β, with Y terms present in the non-Hermitian case
options.B: PT symmetry eliminates transmission and makes only reflection well-defined
options.C: The scattering coefficients require nonlinear matching unavailable for real potentials
options.D: The PT case is equivalent only when every Yₖ vanishes

questions.rationale: The formal scattering structure is unchanged; complex potential data alter α and β.
questions.evidence_quote: transmission and reﬂection coeﬃcients has the same form

questions.question: Which practical caveat about convergence does the discretization discussion emphasize?

options.A: The lattice spacing h and inverse range 1/M are independent small parameters and should be varied independently
options.B: Reducing h automatically fixes truncation error, so M should remain one
options.C: Only M controls the O(h⁴) error; h is a physical parameter that cannot vary
options.D: Increasing h and M together guarantees exact continuum values

questions.rationale: The paper distinguishes discretization error from finite interaction range and recommends independent variation.
